newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold exchange volume hits record.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold exchange volume hits record.

text.p: The Istanbul gold exchange saw record volume on Monday with 2,950 kilos traded compared to Friday's 2,330 kilos and the previous record of 2,570 kilos set on January 8.

"The banks engaged heavily in arbitrage deals and registering imported gold on the exchange, competing to be the one showing the most active trade on the exchange at the end of the month," one dealer said.

Gold closed unchanged in dollar terms at $351.00 an ounce due to the holiday in European markets, but rose in lira terms to 1,442,100 lira per gram from 1,433,400 on Friday as the lira eased against the dollar.
The Turkish currency closed at 127,650 lira to the dollar versus 126,925 lira on Friday's close.
Of the day's trade, most took place in the afternoon session with only 140 kilos changing hands in the morning, and 56.6 percent of trade was conducted in dollar terms.
Bourse members have to register imported gold on the exchange by selling and buying the gold themselves before they can sell it to non-member third parties in the free market.
